kyc-aml-grundlagen-01.question: What was the fundamental change made by the reform of Sec. 261 StGB effective 18 March 2021?

options.a: Money laundering was criminalized in Germany for the first time
options.b: The previous limited catalogue of predicate offenses was replaced with an all-crimes approach
options.c: Money laundering was downgraded from a crime to a mere administrative offense
options.d: Criminal liability was limited to financial institutions only

kyc-aml-grundlagen-01.explanation: Before the reform, Sec. 261 StGB only covered money laundering if the funds derived from an exhaustively enumerated statutory catalogue of predicate offenses. Since 18 March 2021, any unlawful act suffices as a predicate offense (all-crimes approach) - a significant expansion of criminal liability.

kyc-aml-grundlagen-02.question: Which of the following professional groups is explicitly listed as an obligated entity ('Verpflichteter') under Sec. 2(1) GwG?

options.a: Journalists
options.b: Physicians in private practice
options.c: Real estate brokers
options.d: Teachers at public schools

kyc-aml-grundlagen-02.explanation: Sec. 2(1) GwG lists 16 numbered categories of obligated entities, including credit institutions, financial services institutions, insurers, lawyers and notaries (for specified transactions), tax advisors, real estate brokers, and goods dealers. Journalists, private-practice physicians, and public-school teachers are not on this list.

kyc-aml-grundlagen-03.question: What is the basic sanction for recklessly negligent (leichtfertig) money laundering under Sec. 261(6) StGB?

options.a: Imprisonment of up to 2 years, or a fine
options.b: Only a formal warning, no fine
options.c: Imprisonment ranging from at least 6 months to 10 years
options.d: Simple (ordinary) negligent money laundering is punishable just like intentional conduct

kyc-aml-grundlagen-03.explanation: Sec. 261(6) StGB only criminalizes leichtfertig (recklessly/grossly negligent) commission - simple (ordinary) negligence remains unpunishable, an important distinction. The sentencing range for the reckless-negligence offense is far more lenient than for intentional conduct: imprisonment of up to 2 years, or a fine. The 6-month-to-10-year range in option c applies to the especially serious, commercial or gang-based case under Sec. 261(5) StGB.

kyc-aml-grundlagen-04.question: In the classic 3-stage money-laundering model (placement, layering, integration), which step does the 'layering' stage describe?

options.a: The initial introduction of cash into the regular financial system
options.b: A chain of complex transactions designed to obscure the origin of the funds
options.c: The final, seemingly legitimate use of the funds
options.d: A regulator's official report of a suspicious case

kyc-aml-grundlagen-04.explanation: 'Placement' is the introduction stage, 'layering' is the obscuring stage via complex transaction chains, and 'integration' is the final stage where funds re-enter the economy as seemingly legitimate assets. This model is a recognized FATF/BaFin explanatory framework, not a defined statutory term within the GwG itself.

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-01.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the general due diligence duties under Sec. 10(1) GwG?

options.a: Identifying the contracting party
options.b: Determining whether a beneficial owner exists and identifying them
options.c: Obtaining information on the purpose and intended nature of the business relationship
options.d: Automatically reporting the business relationship to the local tax office

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-01.explanation: Sec. 10(1) GwG lists five core duties: identification, determining/identifying the beneficial owner, obtaining information on the purpose and nature of the business relationship, ongoing monitoring including source-of-funds checks, and checking whether the party is a politically exposed person. Automatically reporting the relationship to the tax office is not a GwG due diligence duty.

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-02.question: Above what amount must general due diligence duties be fulfilled for a single, one-off transaction outside an existing business relationship (general threshold under Sec. 10(3) GwG)?

options.a: From EUR 1,000
options.b: From EUR 5,000
options.c: From EUR 15,000
options.d: From EUR 50,000

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-02.explanation: The general threshold under Sec. 10(3) GwG is EUR 15,000. Money transfers and crypto-asset transfers, however, are subject to a markedly lower threshold of EUR 1,000.

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-03.question: Above what amount does the reduced threshold for money transfers and crypto-asset transfers apply under Sec. 10(3) GwG?

options.a: From EUR 1,000
options.b: From EUR 2,000
options.c: From EUR 10,000
options.d: From EUR 15,000

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-03.explanation: Money transfers (per Art. 3 No. 9 of EU Regulation 2023/1113) and crypto-asset transfers are subject to a particularly low threshold of EUR 1,000 - well below the general EUR 15,000 threshold.

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-04.question: A customer carries out a transaction below all applicable thresholds. Must the obligated entity still apply due diligence duties if a concrete suspicion of money laundering exists?

options.a: No, below the thresholds there are generally no duties at all
options.b: Yes, a suspicion of money laundering triggers due diligence duties regardless of any threshold
options.c: Only if the transaction is conducted in cash
options.d: Only after prior approval from BaFin

kyc-aml-sorgfaltspflichten-04.explanation: Besides the value thresholds, Sec. 10(3) GwG provides further triggers independent of any threshold: establishing a business relationship, a concrete suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, and doubts about previously collected identification data. A suspected case therefore overrides any threshold question entirely.

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-01.question: To which authority must an obligated entity submit a suspicious activity report under Sec. 43 GwG?

options.a: The local tax office
options.b: The local police station
options.c: The Financial Intelligence Unit Germany (Zentralstelle für Finanztransaktionsuntersuchungen, FIU)
options.d: The European Central Bank

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-01.explanation: Suspicious activity reports under Sec. 43(1) GwG must be submitted without delay to the Zentralstelle für Finanztransaktionsuntersuchungen (FIU) - Germany's Financial Intelligence Unit - not directly to the tax office, police, or ECB.

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-02.question: Is the reporting duty under Sec. 43 GwG tied to a specific minimum transaction value?

options.a: Yes, a reporting duty only exists from EUR 15,000 upward
options.b: No, the reporting duty exists regardless of the transaction's value
options.c: Yes, but only for cash transactions from EUR 10,000
options.d: No, but only for transactions with a cross-border element

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-02.explanation: Unlike the general due diligence duties, the reporting duty under Sec. 43 GwG has no minimum-amount exemption - if a suspected case exists, a report must be filed without delay regardless of the transaction's value.

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-03.question: What does the 'tipping-off' prohibition under Sec. 47 GwG forbid?

options.a: Informing the affected customer or third parties about a planned or already-filed suspicious activity report
options.b: Internal sharing of suspected cases within the same corporate group
options.c: Cooperation between the FIU and BaFin
options.d: The same obligated entity filing multiple suspicious activity reports

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-03.explanation: Sec. 47 GwG prohibits informing the customer, the transaction party, or third parties about an intended or already-filed report, or about resulting investigations. Group-internal sharing under specified conditions, as well as communication with authorities, are explicitly exempted.

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-04.question: Under what condition does the reporting duty under Sec. 43 GwG exceptionally not apply to lawyers and comparable professions?

options.a: Always - lawyers are generally exempt from the reporting duty entirely
options.b: When the knowledge arose from legal advice/representation - unless the professional themselves knows the advice is being sought specifically for money-laundering purposes
options.c: Only for cases with a value in dispute under EUR 15,000
options.d: Only if the client explicitly objects

kyc-aml-verdachtsmeldung-04.explanation: Sec. 43(2) GwG provides a limited exception for lawyers, notaries, and comparable professions where the relevant knowledge arose from legal advisory or representative activity - what matters is the professional's own knowledge, not the (unprovable) intent of the client: the exception falls away if the professional themselves knows the legal advice is being sought specifically for money-laundering purposes. Note: in certain real-estate matters covered by the GwGMeldV-Immobilien regulation (Sec. 43(6) GwG), this exception can fall away, meaning notaries may face an independent reporting duty there too - the exact scope of that regulation should be confirmed by counsel before relying on it as a firm compliance statement.

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-01.question: Under Sec. 1(12)-(14) GwG, which additional group of people is treated as subject to enhanced scrutiny alongside the politically exposed person (PEP) themselves?

options.a: Only the PEP themselves, never any other person
options.b: Only the PEP's direct superiors in public service
options.c: Only the PEP's former business partners from the past
options.d: Family members and known close associates of the PEP as well

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-01.explanation: Besides the PEP themselves, the GwG also covers family members (Sec. 1(13): spouse/registered partner, children and their partners, parents) and known close associates (Sec. 1(14), e.g. joint beneficial ownership or close business relationships) - both groups are subject to the same enhanced due diligence measures.

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-02.question: Who determines which countries qualify as 'high-risk third countries' for the purposes of Sec. 15 GwG?

options.a: Each obligated entity determines its own list independently
options.b: The GwG statute itself contains a fixed list of countries named in the text
options.c: The European Commission, via a delegated regulation
options.d: The Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-02.explanation: The GwG itself contains no country list of its own - what matters is the list of high-risk third countries determined by the European Commission via a delegated regulation. Obligated entities must rely on this EU list, not on one they create themselves or one issued by the FIU.

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-03.question: What is mandatorily required under Sec. 15(4) GwG before establishing or continuing a business relationship with a politically exposed person?

options.a: Case-by-case approval from BaFin
options.b: Approval from a member of senior management
options.c: Notarization of the business relationship
options.d: A report to the Financial Intelligence Unit before the contract is concluded

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-03.explanation: Sec. 15(4) GwG requires senior-management approval before establishing or continuing a PEP business relationship, appropriate measures to establish the source of wealth/funds, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. This exact requirement was also the subject of a real 2025 BaFin sanction against a German credit institution.

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-04.question: Which characteristic of a transaction typically triggers enhanced due diligence under Sec. 15 GwG, regardless of the parties' country of origin?

options.a: The transaction is especially complex, unusually large, or has no apparent economic or lawful purpose
options.b: The transaction is carried out exclusively by bank transfer rather than in cash
options.c: The transaction is carried out on a weekday
options.d: The transaction is below EUR 1,000

kyc-aml-verstaerkte-sorgfalt-04.explanation: Besides PEP status and high-risk countries, Sec. 15 GwG also names transactions that are especially complex or unusually large, follow an unusual pattern, or show no apparent economic or lawful purpose as an independent trigger - regardless of where the parties involved are from.

kyc-aml-sanktionen-01.question: How high can the fine be for serious, repeated, or systematic violations under Sec. 56(3) GwG for most obligated entities?

options.a: A maximum of EUR 50,000
options.b: Up to EUR 1 million, or twice the economic benefit derived, whichever is higher
options.c: A maximum of EUR 150,000, regardless of severity
options.d: Imprisonment, but no fine

kyc-aml-sanktionen-01.explanation: Sec. 56(3) GwG provides for an aggravated fine framework of up to EUR 1 million, or twice the economic benefit derived from the violation, whichever is higher, for serious, repeated, or systematic violations. An even higher framework applies to credit and financial services institutions (see the next question).

kyc-aml-sanktionen-02.question: What aggravated fine framework applies specifically to credit institutions and financial services institutions for serious violations under Sec. 56(3) GwG?

options.a: The same as all other obligated entities: up to EUR 1 million
options.b: A maximum of EUR 500,000
options.c: Up to EUR 5 million, or 10% of total annual turnover, whichever is higher
options.d: There is no special, higher framework for these institutions

kyc-aml-sanktionen-02.explanation: For credit institutions, financial services institutions, and comparable financial-sector companies, the fine framework for serious, repeated, or systematic violations rises to up to EUR 5 million, or 10% of total annual turnover, whichever is higher. Fines of up to EUR 5 million are also possible for natural persons in this sector.

kyc-aml-sanktionen-03.question: What was the approximate total fine BaFin imposed on KT Bank AG on 23 January 2025 for multiple GwG violations (including inadequate internal safeguards, deficient record-keeping, and missing senior-management approval for PEP relationships)?

options.a: EUR 20,000 in total
options.b: EUR 150,000 in total
options.c: EUR 600,000 in total (30 individual fines of EUR 20,000 each)
options.d: EUR 5 million in total

kyc-aml-sanktionen-03.explanation: On 23 January 2025, BaFin imposed a total fine of EUR 600,000 on KT Bank AG, made up of 30 individual fines of EUR 20,000 each, for violations including Sec. 6(1) (internal safeguards), Sec. 8(4) (record-retention duties), Sec. 10(1) No. 5 and (2) (ongoing monitoring), and Sec. 15(4) No. 1 GwG (missing senior-management approval for PEP business relationships).

kyc-aml-sanktionen-04.question: What is the basic fine framework under Sec. 56(1) GwG for an intentionally committed administrative offense that is not classified as especially serious?

options.a: Up to EUR 10,000
options.b: Up to EUR 150,000
options.c: Up to EUR 1 million
options.d: There is no upper monetary limit

kyc-aml-sanktionen-04.explanation: Sec. 56(1) GwG lists numerous administrative-offense provisions (including violations of risk-assessment, internal-safeguard, or due-diligence requirements) with a base framework of up to EUR 150,000 for intentional conduct, or up to EUR 100,000 for reckless/grossly negligent (leichtfertig) conduct - ordinary negligence does not trigger a fine here. The aggravated framework of up to EUR 1 million (or more for financial institutions) only applies to serious, repeated, or systematic violations under Sec. 56(3) GwG.
